site.description: A law school study library: outlines, rule charts, flowcharts, flashcards, and practice question banks you can open in the browser or download.

subjects.title: Evidence
subjects.description: Federal Rules of Evidence, Weeks 1–15 (Fisher, Evidence, 4th ed.): jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy exclusions, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, the right to present a defense, lay and expert opinion, expert reliability, authentication and the best evidence rule, and privileges. Includes the outline, rule chart, flowcharts, flashcards, and bar-style practice questions.

subjects.title: Professional Responsibility
subjects.description: Model Rules of Professional Conduct, Weeks 1–15 (Burk, Ethical Lawyering, Chs. 1–25): regulating lawyers and bar admission, forming and ending the client-lawyer relationship, competence, confidentiality, agency and fiduciary duty, fees and client funds, conflicts of interest, government lawyers and prosecutors, ethics in advocacy, law firms and organizational clients, public service, duties to third parties, advertising and solicitation, and harassment and discrimination.

subjects.title: Con Law II
subjects.description: Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13). Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, immoral speech, torts involving speech, commercial speech, content-neutral rules and expressive conduct, government speech, funding and forum doctrine, government employees and public schools, and social media and elections.

subjects.title: Sales and Leases
subjects.description: Sales and Leases of Goods under UCC Articles 1, 2 and 2A, Weeks 1–14 (Sepinuck, Chapters 1–7, 9 and 11). Covers which law governs, formation and the battle of the forms, the statute of frauds, warranties and disclaimers, gap fillers, delivery and risk of loss, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, repudiation, excuse, buyer's and seller's remedies, rejection, cure and revocation, privity, and leases under Article 2A.

subjects.title: Agency & Partnership
subjects.description: Business Associations, Weeks 1–8 (Bainbridge, Park & Rodrigues, 6th ed.). Covers creating an agency, actual and apparent authority, ratification and estoppel, a principal's tort liability, agents' fiduciary duties, choosing an entity, partnership formation under the UPA and RUPA, partners' rights, authority and duties, dissociation and dissolution, loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs.

subjects.title: Contracts I
subjects.description: Contracts I, Weeks 1–9 (Epstein, Markell & Ponoroff, Making and Doing Deals, 7th ed.). Covers whether there is an enforceable agreement, the objective theory of assent, offers and their termination, options and firm offers, methods of acceptance and silence, the mirror-image rule and UCC § 2-207, misunderstanding, indefiniteness and letters of intent, consideration, modification, promissory estoppel, the statute of frauds, duress, and misrepresentation.

subjects.title: Civil Procedure
subjects.description: Civil Procedure, Weeks 1–9 (Spencer, Civil Procedure: A Contemporary Approach, 7th ed., and the Federal Civil Rules Supplement). Covers the court systems and sources of procedural law, personal jurisdiction from Pennoyer through Ford, notice and service of process under Rule 4, federal question, diversity, supplemental and removal jurisdiction, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, the Erie doctrine through Shady Grove, pleading standards from Conley to Iqbal, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint under Rules 8, 12, and 55.

subjects.title: Torts
subjects.description: Torts, Weeks 1–15 (Prosser, Wade & Schwartz, Torts: Cases and Materials, keyed to the 13th ed.). Covers liability based on fault, the intentional torts and their privileges, negligence (the reasonable person, professionals, negligence per se, proof, and res ipsa loquitur), cause in fact and proximate cause, duty and the failure to act, comparative fault, assumption of risk, limitations and immunities, premises liability, compensatory and punitive damages, joint and several liability, contribution, vicarious liability, strict liability, and nuisance.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence Outline
documents.description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–1098). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Part IX covers expert bases and reliability (703, 705, Frye, Daubert, Joiner, Kumho Tire). Part X covers authentication and the best evidence rule (901–902, 1001–1008). Part XI covers Rule 501, the psychotherapist and lawyer-client privileges, 502 waiver, government lawyers, and self-incrimination. Part XII covers the spousal and marital-confidences privileges. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.

documents.description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Burk, Ethical Lawyering, Chs. 1–25, and the Model Rules with their Comments), in syllabus order. Part I covers regulating lawyers: sources of law, bar admission and discipline, unauthorized practice, the consequences of misconduct, and why smart people do stupid things. Part II covers the MR 1.0 definitions, competence and diligence, the duty of care and ineffective assistance, forming the relationship, scope, duties to non-clients, clients with decision-making limitations (MR 1.14), and declining and withdrawing. Part III covers confidentiality, privilege and work product, and the MR 1.6(b) exceptions. Part IV covers the lawyer as fiduciary and agent, candor under MR 1.4, and the allocation of authority. Part V covers fees, retainers, fee sharing, and trust accounts. Part VI covers conflicts: personal-interest conflicts under MR 1.8, concurrent and former clients, imputation and screening, and consent. Part VII covers government lawyers, the revolving door (MR 1.11, 1.12), and prosecutors (MR 3.8). Part VIII covers ethics in advocacy (MR 2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.9). Part IX covers supervision in law firms, selling a practice, and organizational clients (MR 1.13). Part X covers public service (MR 6.1–6.5). Part XI covers truthfulness, represented and unrepresented persons, client wrongdoing, threats and reporting, restrictions on practice, and advertising and solicitation. Part XII covers MR 8.4(g), and Part XIII has review tables for the final. Rule and tip boxes throughout, the class quiz answers for Chs. 22, 24, and 25 worked in, and case cards for the cases the readings rely on, including the assigned Bradwell and Zauderer.

documents.description: 255 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and tip in the Weeks 1–9 outline (Classes 1–16), across 15 topics: the court systems and sources of procedural law, the personal jurisdiction framework and territorial era, minimum contacts, specific jurisdiction and the stream of commerce, general, consent, and tag jurisdiction, notice and service under Rule 4, federal question, diversity and alienage, supplemental jurisdiction, removal, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, Swift to Erie, the modern Erie analysis, pleading and Rule 11, and responding to the complaint, plus a set of integrated multi-issue problems. Each question is an MBE-style fact pattern that asks what a court should do. The four choices are written to the same length and form, and the wrong ones are the usual bar traps: the right result for the wrong reason, a correct rule that does not apply, and a misstated rule. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.

documents.title: Torts Outline
documents.description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus, in syllabus order. The syllabus assigns the 15th edition of Prosser, Wade & Schwartz; the outline follows the 13th edition and maps each reading to its 13th-ed. chapter and cases. Part I covers the move from strict liability to fault. Parts II and III cover intent, battery, assault, false imprisonment, IIED, trespass to land and chattels, conversion, and the privileges: consent, self-defense, defense of others and of property, recapture, the shopkeeper's privilege, necessity, and discipline. Parts IV and V cover the negligence case, the Hand formula, the reasonable person, professionals and informed consent, negligence per se, notice, and res ipsa loquitur. Part VI covers but-for and substantial-factor causation, lost chance, alternative and market share liability, proximate cause, and superseding causes. Part VII covers duty and the failure to act. Part VIII covers comparative fault, assumption of risk, limitations, and immunities. Parts IX through XIV cover premises liability, damages, joint and several liability and contribution, vicarious liability, strict liability, and nuisance, and Part XV has review tables for the final. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a case card for each principal case in the assigned pages. The Canvas-only readings are not briefed.

documents.title: Restatement (Third) of Torts: Miscellaneous Provisions
documents.description: The Restatement (Third) of Torts: Miscellaneous Provisions sections the outline relies on, from Tentative Draft No. 3 (2024). Statutes of limitations and repose (§§ 1–16), aiding and abetting negligence, agreements to act negligently, the firefighter's rule, and liability for providing alcohol come with their black letter, Comments, and Illustrations. The Sections the ALI approved in 2022 come as black letter: apportionment (§§ 4 A–4 B and 27–37), immunities (§§ 1–10A), and loss of consortium (§§ 48 A–48 C). Search by word or section number, filter by outline topic, and open or close the Comments.
